mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive sequential revision in personal savings (RSAFS) combined with a decline in consumer spending (proxied by HOUST) indicates a shift from consumption to saving, which typically precedes a slowdown in economic activity and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS revision > 0 and HOUST < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) of more than 10% during a period of rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS > previous year) signals a housing market contraction under restrictive monetary policy, which drags on construction-related equities and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY change < -10% and FEDFUNDS > previous year
regime_hint: housing market contraction with restrictive policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
